maria_acme: Hey team — onboarding question. We're trying to use Azure Key Vault with Redwood BYOK + envelope encryption. Docs are a bit light on required RBAC and the exact permissions Redwood needs on the key. Also want to confirm how key rotation should work (we rotate quarterly). Can someone advise?

jess_support: Hi Maria — welcome! :wave: We'll get this sorted. Quick Qs: do you plan to give Redwood a service principal that has access to the key, or will you run a proxy in your VPC?

maria_acme: We'll create a service principal in our tenant and grant it permissions to the specific key. No proxy.

sam_security: Thanks. For Azure Key Vault when using envelope encryption (Redwood holds only ciphertext of data keys), the SPN needs the crypto permissions on the key: encrypt, decrypt, wrapKey, unwrapKey. If you use signing for attestation also sign/verify. In IAM role terms that's the built-in role "Key Vault Crypto User" or a custom role with these actions: 
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/encrypt/action
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/decrypt/action
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrapKey/action
- Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrapKey/action

sam_security: Also we require Get/list on key metadata so Redwood can detect key versions: Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/get/list/action

lee_devops: For validation we usually ask for the key identifier (full URI), the key version you want to use, and the SPN client id + tenant id (we never store secrets in clear). We'll give you a short validation script to run once the SPN is granted permissions.

maria_acme: Got it. About key rotation — if we rotate the key (create new version) every 90 days, will Redwood automatically pick up the new version? Any rewrap steps required?

sam_security: Good question. Azure Key Vault key rotation creates new key versions under the same key name. Redwood looks at the key URI + optional pinned version. By default we follow the latest enabled version. When you rotate keys we will automatically start using new versions for new data keys. Important caveat: you must keep old versions enabled for decrypting existing envelopes OR provide a rewrap job to re-encrypt old data keys with the new version. If your policy disables or purges old versions, you will lose the ability to decrypt past ciphertexts.

jess_support: Short checklist for Azure BYOK onboarding: 
1) Create Key Vault and key (RSA/HSM-backed recommended).
2) Create service principal, grant it Key Vault Crypto User on the key + Get/list on keys.
3) Provide Redwood the key URI (and optional version) and SPN client id + tenant id. We'll provide an upload URL for the SPN credential (client secret) to our private onboarding vault.
4) Enable Azure diagnostic logs for Key Vault (Audit) and forward to a storage/monitoring project we can validate.

lee_devops: For rotation workflow we recommend either: 
- Let Azure auto-rotate versions and keep versions enabled (Redwood will decrypt with old versions automatically).
- Or schedule a rewrap: 1) use Redwood tooling to re-encrypt stored data keys with the new key version; 2) validate decrypts; 3) retire old versions only after verification.

maria_acme: For AWS and GCP customers we also had to enable CloudTrail/audit logs. What's Redwood's requirement for audit logging here?

audit_bot: Redwood requirement (short): KMS API calls (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/Wrap/Unwrap) must be logged and retained for at least 90 days. Provide one of: CloudTrail (AWS) with KMS events, Cloud Audit Logs (GCP) for Cloud KMS, Azure Diagnostic Logs for Key Vault. We need read access (or an exported sample) for onboarding validation.

sam_security: Adding a few quick CLI checks you can run after SPN permissions are granted: 
Azure CLI examples:
```bash
# test encrypt/decrypt (replace placeholders)
az keyvault key encrypt --vault-name my-vault --name my-key --algorithm RSA-OAEP --value "aGVsbG8=" | jq -r .result > cipher.b64
az keyvault key decrypt --vault-name my-vault --name my-key --algorithm RSA-OAEP --value $(cat cipher.b64) | jq -r .result
```
The result should round-trip to the original base64 plaintext.

# quick permission check (Graph API)
az role assignment list --assignee <SPN_CLIENT_ID> --scope /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<vault>/keys/<key>

lee_devops: For AWS (if they ask later) minimal IAM for an IAM role/user: kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt, kms:DescribeKey, kms:GetPublicKey (if asymmetric). For GCP: roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key ring/key.

jess_support: Documentation gap noted: we'll add a table in the BYOK guide listing exact permissions per cloud and a short rotation FAQ. Filing the doc ticket now.

jess_support: Maria — if you can DM the key URI and create a short audit logs snapshot (or give us a read-only view), we can run the validation within the next 24 hours. Also send the SPN client id + tenant id so we can verify role assignment. We'll ask you to upload the SPN secret to the onboarding upload URL when ready.

maria_acme: Thanks — I'll prepare the info and share it in DM. One last security question: do you require HSM-backed keys only?

sam_security: We strongly prefer HSM-backed keys for customer-managed keys (Azure HSM, AWS KMS with symmetric CMK, or Google Cloud HSM). We allow software keys in exceptional cases but require documented exception and higher audit retention.

maria_acme: Perfect. Thanks all!

kms_bot: [system] Validation checklist queued (id: onboard-9981). Expect status updates in this thread once Jess kicks off the run.

jess_support: I'll start the validation once I have the DM info. Marking this as in-progress. :white_check_mark:
